Nematodes can both increase and decrease soil fertility depending on the species: some beneficial nematodes enhance nutrient cycling by breaking down organic matter and releasing nutrients [d1][d3], while plant-parasitic nematodes feed on plant roots, damaging the root system and reducing nutrient uptake even if external fertilizers are applied [d4]. Fertilizer type further modulates these effects—organic fertilizers tend to increase free-living nematode populations and nutrient availability, whereas inorganic fertilizers can negatively affect nematode communities, particularly plant-parasitic species [d5]. Research also shows that the interaction between tillage and fertilization significantly influences soil nematode abundance and community structure [d2], making the overall impact of nematodes on soil fertility a complex, context-dependent process.
[[END-OF-ANSWER]]
